title: Independent adversarial review of the F6-R1 publication-window fix in Story 1.2
summary: Perform a fresh read-only adversarial review of the Story 1.2 mutation-lock protocol after the F6-R1 correction, in which afk_lock_acquire now waits out the transient post-mkdir pre-owner.json publication window inside a bounded observation budget instead of classifying it OPERATION_LOCK_OWNER_UNVERIFIABLE and advising removal of a possibly live lock. Independently attack the publication window itself, stale reclamation, N-way contention on clean and contended lock paths, owner/reclaimer interleavings, former-owner release after successor acquisition, process death during acquire/reclaim/release, identity changes between observation and action, and every prior F6 scenario. Specifically evaluate the implementer's self-reported residual risk: a lost arbitration marker vanishing between its existence check and its judge makes reclaim return 2, so a loser can still be told to remove a lock a successor may hold — judge whether that is a Story 1.2-owned blocker. Construct and run hostile multiprocess interleavings, inspect for asymmetric or bypass paths, verify the new forced-window and clean-lock regressions are genuine and anti-vacuous, and independently rerun every Story 1.2 deterministic gate including git diff --check. Report findings only; do not modify repository files.
